## Code review

Reviewed at `9a43734`. The mechanism is sound and well-fitted to the existing code — extending the quality-preset system rather than bolting on a separate mobile renderer or UA sniffing is the right call, and every build/test claim in the description reproduces. Two of the automatic-selection heuristics don't do what the description says they do, though, and I'd want both addressed before this leaves draft.

### Claims verified

Reproduced on this branch:

- `vitest run` — 180 files, 1191 tests passing (description says 1,190)
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `eslint .` — 0 errors, 9 warnings
- `next build` — succeeds

The tier wiring also does what it claims. With a stored tier on a 412×915 DPR-3 profile, reading the live context attributes off the scene canvas:

| stored tier | antialias | drawing buffer | effective DPR |
|---|---|---|---|
| low | `false` | 412×915 | 1.0 |
| balanced | `true` | 618×1372 | 1.5 |
| ultra | `true` | 824×1830 | 2.0 |

The stored override correctly beats automatic selection, and I saw no hydration errors despite `resolveInitialGraphicsQuality()` running in a `useState` initializer inside a server-prerendered client component.

### 1. Landscape phones never reach the Low tier

`resolveAutomaticGraphicsQuality` gates the mobile path on `viewportWidth <= 768` measured from `window.innerWidth`, so a phone held sideways falls through to Balanced. Measured in Chromium device emulation against the real `/office` page (`softwareRenderer` forced false to isolate the new logic):

| device | `innerWidth` | coarse pointer | reduced motion | automatic tier |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| desktop 1440×900 | 1440 | false | false | balanced |
| desktop 1440×900 reduced-motion | 1440 | false | true | **low** |
| Pixel 7 portrait | 412 | true | false | low |
| Pixel 7 landscape | 915 | true | false | **balanced** |
| iPhone 14 Pro portrait | 393 | true | false | low |
| iPhone 14 Pro landscape | 852 | true | false | **balanced** |

Since selection happens once at mount and is never re-evaluated, a user who loads the page in landscape stays on the heavy preset for the entire session. `Math.min(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight) <= 768` would cover both orientations.

(Worth noting these numbers require loading the real page — on `about:blank` Chromium reports its 980px fallback layout viewport because there's no viewport meta tag, which makes every mobile profile look like it selects Balanced for the wrong reason.)

### 2. Mapping `prefers-reduced-motion` to the Low tier is the wrong lever

This preference is introduced by this PR and is used nowhere else in the app, so its only effect is to strip visual fidelity — shadows, MSAA, ambient occlusion, bloom, SMAA, and DPR — from users who asked for less animation.

It also barely reduces motion. Agents keep walking, `DaylightDrift` keeps swinging and recoloring the sun every frame because it sits outside the `config.decorativeMotion` gate, and camera easing still runs. The only motion actually removed is `DustMotes`.

This also makes "Balanced and Ultra desktop defaults visually unchanged" untrue for these users: a high-end desktop that sets reduced-motion now boots into Low. Suggest keeping tier selection on capability signals only, and adding a separate `reducedMotion` flag that gates the animated systems (`DustMotes`, `DaylightDrift`, camera easing).

### Smaller notes

**`resolveRenderDpr`'s 0.75 floor is inert.** It conflicts with the 0.85 minimum declared in `dpr={[0.85, graphicsQualityConfig.maxDpr]}` and used as `minDpr` in `AdaptiveDprController`. R3F re-applies the tuple on Canvas re-render, so 0.75 never reaches the renderer — at `devicePixelRatio` 0.5 the measured effective DPR is 0.85. That makes the `expect(resolveRenderDpr(0.5, 2)).toBe(0.75)` assertion cover a value the renderer never uses. Either drop the floor or make it 0.85 so there's one minimum.

**`shouldRunAnimationFrame` is close to a no-op.** Browsers already suspend `requestAnimationFrame` for hidden documents. It's harmless — `tick` is wall-clock based via `Date.now()`, so skipping frames can't desync anything — but it isn't the pause the description implies, and it adds a per-frame `document.visibilityState` read.

**Stale user-facing copy.** Low's entry in `GRAPHICS_QUALITY_OPTIONS` still reads "No post-processing, small shadow maps" even though Low no longer casts shadows at all, which also makes its `shadowMapSize: 512` dead config. Existing users who already stored Low will silently lose shadows on upgrade.

**Nit:** the new test file is missing a trailing newline.

**Not a concern:** adding `graphicsQuality` to the Canvas `key` is correct and necessary since `antialias` is immutable per WebGL context, and it isn't a new source of churn — `canvasResetKey` already contains `String(agents.length)`, so the canvas remounts whenever the agent count changes. I hit that repeatedly while testing.

### On the remaining validation

The stated need for a real-device pass is genuine rather than a formality. On a GPU-less software renderer, Balanced paints nothing within 30 seconds, and I confirmed that's pre-existing by reproducing it on `main` — so the maintainer visual review of the Low-tier tradeoff genuinely cannot be produced in a SwiftShader environment.

<sub>Review performed by a Cursor cloud agent: read-only inspection plus reruns of the existing test, typecheck, lint, and build commands, with Chromium device-emulation measurements against a local dev server and the bundled demo gateway. No code was changed.</sub>

## Code review

Reviewed at `a5803ad` (73 files, +6,898/−909). A lot of this is careful work — `pr-delivery.js` in particular does the right things (`spawnSync` with `shell: false`, array argv, worktree containment, branch verification, refuses the default branch, no force push, token redaction in errors), and `resolveFleetAvatarAsset` is a textbook-correct path guard. But there is one newly introduced issue I'd treat as release-blocking, plus a portability bug that breaks the managed-fleet feature outright on Linux/macOS.

### 1. Arbitrary host file read/write via the new `agents.files.*` handlers (blocking)

`server/hermes-agent/bridge.js` adds `agents.files.get` / `agents.files.set` and `resolveAgentFilePath(agentId, fileName)`, which joins both parameters into `~/.hermes/profiles/<agentId>/<name>` with no validation or containment check. Both parameters come straight off the wire.

I confirmed all three primitives against the branch by driving the bridge's own `upstream.send`:

```
profile dir the handler intends to confine writes to:
   /home/ubuntu/.hermes/profiles/default

--- 1. arbitrary write via agents.files.set ---
params.name = ../../../../../tmp/hermes3d-pr26-arbitrary-write.txt
--- 2. arbitrary read via agents.files.get ---
params.name = ../../../../../tmp/hermes3d-pr26-secret.txt
--- 3. managed-profile write guard bypass ---
params.agentId = default (unmanaged), params.name = ../managed-agent/SOUL.md

================ RESULT ================
write escaped profile dir : YES -> /tmp/hermes3d-pr26-arbitrary-write.txt
  file contents           : "written outside the profile directory by agents.files.set\n"
read escaped profile dir  : YES -> "SIMULATED-PRIVATE-KEY-CONTENTS\n"
managed SOUL.md written   : YES -> /home/ubuntu/.hermes/profiles/managed-agent/SOUL.md
```

The read path also echoes the resolved absolute path back to the caller, which makes it a convenient filesystem probe.

Note the third line: this defeats the read-only Brain enforcement this PR is adding. `isManagedFleetAgent()` only inspects `agentId`, so an **unmanaged** `agentId` plus a traversing `name` writes into a managed agent's Brain files anyway.

On reachability: `createHermesAgentUpstream` is used **embedded in-process** by `gateway-proxy.js`, so these methods sit behind the browser-facing `/api/gateway/ws`. `browserWs.on("message")` forwards any `type: "req"` frame to `upstream.send`, which dispatches to `handleMethod` with no method allowlist, and the file handlers never touch the upstream. The access gate is disabled unless `STUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set (`enabled = Boolean(token)`), and there is no `Origin` check on the WebSocket upgrade — WebSocket handshakes aren't subject to CORS, so while the hermes-agent adapter is active, any page the developer has open can drive this.

Suggested fix: validate `name` against a fixed allowlist (the `MANAGED_FILES` list in `managedProfiles.ts` is already the right set) or at minimum `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` plus a `path.basename(name) === name` check; validate `agentId` the same way; then resolve and confine to the profile root. That's exactly the pattern `resolveFleetAvatarAsset` already uses correctly in this PR. Separately, an `Origin` check on the `/api/gateway/ws` upgrade would be worth adding regardless.

### 2. `python` is hardcoded, which breaks managed fleet on POSIX (blocking)

`runFleetCommand` in `src/lib/fleet/managedProfiles.ts` calls `execFile("python", ...)`. Per PEP 394 most Linux and macOS installs provide only `python3`, so every fleet command fails there — `validate`, `diff`, `apply`, `rollback`, and the implicit `reconcile`.

This is also why the verification claim doesn't hold on a non-Windows host. `tests/unit/managedProfiles.test.ts` fails:

```
AssertionError: expected null to deeply equal { counts: {}, tasks: [] }
❯ tests/unit/managedProfiles.test.ts:107:32
```

`readRecovery()` shells out, `execFile` fails with ENOENT, stdout is empty, `JSON.parse("")` throws, and `recovery` comes back `null`. Suggest resolving an interpreter (`HERMES3D_PYTHON`, else `python3`, else `python`) and surfacing a clear error when none is found.

### 3. `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` is checked for presence but never compared

`authorizeFleetRequest` reads like authentication, but it only verifies the env var is *non-empty* — the value is never compared against anything from the request. What actually gates the endpoint is a static `x-hermes3d-fleet-session: 1` header plus `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site` checks that are **skipped entirely when those headers are absent**, which is the case for any non-browser client. That combination is a reasonable CSRF defense (the custom header forces a preflight that no CORS handler answers) but it is not authentication, and the commit message "guard managed fleet APIs to local sessions" suggests something stronger was intended — there's no loopback check either. Either compare the token or rename the helper and comments so a future reader doesn't over-trust it.

### 4. The validate → preview → apply interlock isn't enforced server-side

`src/app/api/fleet/route.ts` gates `apply` on `body.validatedHash === fleet.sourceHash && body.previewedHash === fleet.sourceHash`, but the client supplies both values and `sourceHash` is handed out by `GET /api/fleet`. Any caller can send the current hash twice and apply immediately without ever running validate or diff. That's fine as UI ergonomics; if it's meant to be a safety control, the server has to remember that validate and diff actually ran.

### 5. `/api/fleet/assets/[asset]` has no authorization

Every other fleet surface goes through `authorizeFleetRequest`, and commit 6d661c3 adds the session header to the *client* fetch, but the route itself never checks it — so the assets the PR describes as private are served unauthenticated. The path handling is correctly confined, so this is access control only, not traversal. Minor: `readFile` isn't wrapped, so a file removed between `resolveFleetAvatarAsset` and the read produces an unhandled rejection rather than a 404.

### 6. CSP: `'unsafe-eval'` is now enabled in production

`next.config.ts` previously dropped `'unsafe-eval'` outside dev; it's now unconditional. The comment directly above it still reads "In production it is dropped — React and Three.js do not need eval", so code and comment now contradict each other. If this was needed for WASM (Draco, Phaser), `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` is sufficient on its own and is already in the list — worth confirming whether the broader token can come back out.

### 7. `isManagedFleetAgent` fails open

`server/managed-fleet.js` returns an empty set whenever `fleet-status.json` is missing, unreadable, or invalid JSON, which makes every managed agent writable again. For a control whose purpose is preventing drift from direct Brain edits, failing closed when `HERMES3D_FLEET_ROOT` is configured seems safer, with the error surfaced instead of swallowed.

### 8. PR delivery defaults to a very broad workspace root

`defaultWorkspaceRoot()` falls back to `path.dirname(process.cwd())` — the parent of the checkout — so every sibling git repo is an eligible delivery target. Meanwhile `standupDispatch.ts` stamps `[hermes3d:github-pr]` into the description of *every* standup task, and `isPullRequestDeliveryCandidate` only needs that marker plus `review` status and a branch. Net effect: agent-generated standup content can cause a branch push and a PR opened with host credentials in any repo next to Hermes3D. The containment checks all work correctly; it's the default root that's wide. I'd require `HERMES3D_PR_WORKSPACE_ROOT` explicitly rather than defaulting.

### Smaller notes

**New lint error.** `src/features/office/phaser/OfficeBuilderScene.ts:96` introduces `(existing as any).geom`, tripping `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`. The repo was at 0 errors before this branch (`eslint .` reports 12 problems / 1 error here vs 9 problems / 0 errors on `main`). The accompanying empty `try {} catch {}` also swallows every failure, and the `geom` guard papers over a Phaser state that isn't explained — a typed narrowing plus a comment on why `geom` can be absent would age better.

**A `GET /api/fleet` spawns a Python subprocess.** `readManagedFleetSnapshot()` always calls `readRecovery()` → `fleet.py reconcile`. `useManagedFleetProfile.refresh` also depends on `validatedHash`, so a successful validate re-runs the effect and refetches, spawning another subprocess with a 30s timeout. Worth caching, or at least making recovery opt-in per request. Relatedly: `reconcile` runs on a plain GET without passing through the `mutationsEnabled` gate that `apply`/`rollback` require — if `reconcile` can mutate anything, that's a gap.

**`parseGitHubRepoSlug` can return a leading-dash slug.** A remote of `https://github.com/-x/y` satisfies `/^[^/]+\/[^/]+$/`, and the result is passed to `gh` as argv where it would parse as flags. There's no shell involved so this isn't injection, and it needs control of a remote inside the workspace root, but a `--` separator or a stricter character class is nearly free.

**Hand-rolled `.env` parser.** The loader added to `server/index.js` doesn't strip surrounding quotes, so `KEY="value"` yields a value with literal quote characters — an easy way to get a confusing token mismatch. Real environment variables correctly take precedence, which is good.

**Loopback upstreams are now allowed in production.** `isUpstreamAllowed` returns true for `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`::1` before the production `UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST` refusal that previously applied. Convenient locally, but it lets a browser ask the server to open WebSockets to arbitrary local ports in a production build.

**`docker rename` on containers this app didn't create.** It's opt-in behind `HERMES3D_READABLE_DOCKER_NAMES` and the sanitizing and legacy-name matching are careful, but renaming containers another system owns can break that system's name-based lookups; worth a warning in the module docs.

### Verification on this branch

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean (exit 0) |
| `next build` | succeeds |
| `vitest run` | **1 failed**, 1235 passed (187 files) — `managedProfiles.test.ts`, cause in finding 2 |
| `eslint .` | **1 error**, 11 warnings (was 0 errors / 9 warnings on `main`) |

So `typecheck` and `build` match the description. The test claim ("1230 passed; one Windows-environment-only symlink test could not create a symlink") doesn't reproduce here: the failure I see is not the symlink test but the fleet recovery assertion, and it stems from a real portability bug rather than the environment. Lint isn't mentioned in the description and does regress.

No repository files were modified; the PoC wrote only to temp paths and cleaned up after itself.</sub>
Hi @iamlukethedev - gentle nudge on this one and #33 whenever you have a minute. Both are small and still merge cleanly, and I am happy to adjust either if you would prefer a different approach.

Adding a few data points from running Hermes3D at `beb7629` against hermes-agent 0.21.6 on Linux. They don't explain the `npm run dev` case above (the allowlist below is only enforced when `NODE_ENV=production`), but they end in the same stuck "Connecting…" screen, so they may help others who land here.

1. **Production builds (`npm start`, Docker): an empty `UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST` blocks every upstream without telling the UI.** `server/gateway-proxy.js` refuses the connection when `UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST` is empty and `NODE_ENV=production`. The server logs `refusing upstream connection: UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST is empty in production` and `connect failed (studio.gateway_url_blocked)`, but the office only shows "Connecting…". The variable isn't in `.env.example`. Setting `UPSTREAM_ALLOWLIST=127.0.0.1,localhost` fixed it for both the demo gateway and a loopback `hermes serve`.

2. **Recent hermes-agent runs one backend per host.** A second `hermes serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120`, as in `docs/hermes-agent-tailscale.md`, refuses to start when the host already runs a backend on another address (exit 78, see `_attach_to_host_backend` in `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py`). `hermes serve --isolated --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120` starts a dedicated loopback backend that the host never adopts. With that, `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_TYPE=hermes-agent` and `HERMES3D_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:9120` were enough on this commit: the embedded bridge appended `/api/ws?token=…` itself, and every profile showed up as an agent.

3. **Stale browser state.** After switching the same browser from the demo backend to hermes-agent, `/office` stayed on "Loading…" until I cleared the origin's `localStorage`. A fresh tab connected immediately. This may be related to the stale `officeFloors` state described above.
Closing this — I've decided not to pursue it. Sorry for the noise, and thanks for Hermes3D.
